summary: Private VPC pilot: intermittent DNS resolution in private subnets impacting core services (EKS/CoreDNS, VPC endpoints)
description:
Issue summary
- Northstar Healthcare pilot (Private/VPC) is seeing intermittent DNS failures from workloads running in private subnets.
- Symptoms: sporadic resolution failures for both internal cluster names (kubernetes.default, CoreDNS upstream lookups) and AWS service domains (ecr.*, sts.*, logs.*) when VPC endpoints/private DNS are in play.
- Impact: cluster add-ons and Redwood Private installer pods occasionally fail to pull images / reach AWS APIs; some core services restart due to readiness/liveness probe failures when upstream lookups time out.

Impact
- Customer reports that failures appear in bursts (5–20 minutes), then self-resolve.
- During bursts:
  - Image pulls intermittently fail (i/o timeout, no such host)
  - Installer preflight checks sometimes fail on STS/CloudWatch Logs reachability
  - Internal service discovery occasionally fails (CoreDNS returns SERVFAIL)
- Customer severity: blocking stable POC validation; they cannot proceed to the next security gate until stability is demonstrated.

Customer environment
- AWS: us-east-1
- EKS: private subnets across 3 AZs
- VPC endpoints enabled for ECR (api + dkr), S3 gateway endpoint, STS, CloudWatch Logs (and others per our alpha guidance)
- No direct internet egress from private subnets (very strict egress controls); NAT exists but is not used for most traffic per customer policy
- Customer DNS: Route 53 Resolver is default; they also have conditional forwarding requirements to on-prem (future state), but for this pilot they stated no active Resolver rules should be affecting *.amazonaws.com

Timeline (customer-reported)
- 2025-07-07: first observed during cluster bootstrap
- 2025-07-08: escalated to Redwood during pilot standup; ticket opened
- 2025-07-10: joint troubleshooting session; captured CoreDNS + node-level logs
- 2025-07-15: mitigation validated; customer reports no further bursts for 72 hours

Steps to reproduce (as observed)
1) Deploy standard cluster add-ons and Redwood Private prerequisites in private subnets.
2) Run parallel image pulls from ECR and make repeated DNS queries from pods (dig/nslookup) to:
   - kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local
   - ecr.api.<region>.amazonaws.com
   - sts.<region>.amazonaws.com
3) During burst windows, observe intermittent failures:
   - nslookup returns SERVFAIL or times out
   - curl to AWS APIs fails with "Could not resolve host" from within pods

What we checked (investigation notes)
- Confirmed issue reproduces from multiple nodes across AZs; not isolated to a single node.
- CoreDNS:
  - Metrics showed spikes in upstream query latency and timeouts during burst windows.
  - CoreDNS logs included intermittent: "plugin/errors: 2 <domain> A: read udp <pod_ip>:<port>-><upstream_dns>:53: i/o timeout".
- Node / VPC resolver path:
  - Verified /etc/resolv.conf inside pods points to the cluster DNS service (typical).
  - Verified CoreDNS upstream configured to use VPC resolver.
  - Confirmed VPC attributes enableDnsSupport/enableDnsHostnames are enabled (customer had enableDnsHostnames = false initially; they flipped it during troubleshooting per Victor’s request).
- Network controls:
  - Customer NACLs are restrictive; one NACL rule set did not include ephemeral return traffic for UDP 53 flows from private subnets to the VPC resolver.
  - Observed that when NACLs were loosened temporarily, DNS bursts reduced significantly.
- VPC endpoints + private DNS:
  - Noticed customer enabled private DNS on endpoints but had not enabled the corresponding endpoint security group ingress from all node/pod CIDRs (they were allowing from node SG only).
  - During some bursts, DNS would resolve to private endpoint IPs, but follow-on connections would fail, creating the impression of DNS instability.
- EKS add-on posture:
  - CoreDNS was deployed at default replica count for their cluster size; during transient network issues, CoreDNS became a bottleneck.

Working hypothesis
- Primary driver: restrictive NACL + missing ephemeral return rules leading to intermittent UDP/53 failures between CoreDNS and the VPC resolver, exacerbated under bursty lookup load.
- Secondary contributors:
  - Endpoint SG allow-listing was too narrow (node SG only), which broke traffic from some pods (depending on CNI/pod IP allocation).
  - CoreDNS capacity too low and retry behavior amplified the issue during partial packet loss.

Evidence / logs (sanitized)
- CoreDNS (during burst):
  - "plugin/errors: 2 ecr.api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com. A: read udp 10.20.34.18:38842->10.10.0.2:53: i/o timeout"
  - "SERVFAIL" responses for external names, intermittent
- Pod-level:
  - "nslookup: can't resolve 'sts.us-east-1.amazonaws.com'"
  - "docker login" / image pull errors: "lookup <ecr-host> on <cluster-dns-ip>:53: no such host"

Mitigation applied (confirmed with customer)
1) NACL updates (customer-owned)
- Ensure NACL rules allow:
  - Outbound UDP/TCP 53 from node/pod CIDRs to VPC resolver (VPC+2 address) within VPC
  - Return traffic for ephemeral ports (1024-65535) for UDP/TCP response flows
- Customer implemented recommended ephemeral allow rules scoped to VPC CIDR.

2) VPC resolver / VPC attributes sanity
- Confirmed VPC attributes:
  - enableDnsSupport = true
  - enableDnsHostnames = true
- Confirm DHCP option set uses AmazonProvidedDNS (no custom DNS servers for pilot).

3) Endpoint SG allow-listing
- Updated endpoint security groups to allow inbound from:
  - EKS node security group
  - Pod CIDR(s) if pods have routable VPC IPs (AWS VPC CNI), or relevant source CIDRs
- This addressed the “DNS resolves but connect fails” confusion for AWS API endpoints.

4) CoreDNS resiliency
- Increased CoreDNS replicas (customer changed from 2 -> 4) and enabled anti-affinity across AZs.
- Added request/limits to prevent CPU starvation.
- Optional (not required for resolution): consider NodeLocal DNSCache for larger clusters; customer deferred.

Outcome
- Customer reports no further DNS bursts for 72 hours after changes.
- Redwood installer preflight checks and image pulls stabilized.

Redwood follow-ups (docs/modules)
- Action: update alpha Terraform module docs to make DNS/NACL expectations explicit.
  - Add a dedicated “DNS prerequisites and failure modes” section (CoreDNS upstream to VPC resolver, NACL ephemeral returns, VPC attributes).
  - Clarify that VPC endpoints SGs must allow pod CIDRs when using AWS VPC CNI.
  - Add a troubleshooting checklist: verify enableDnsSupport/enableDnsHostnames, DHCP options, NACL ephemeral rules, and endpoint SG sources.
- Proposed doc updates to land in: vpc-terraform-modules alpha deployment guide + reference architecture.
  - Owner: Kira Thompson to draft; review by Victor Alvarez + Sean Gallagher.

Notes / cross-links
- Related support pattern: missing endpoints and private DNS misconfig causing ECR failures (see SUP-28411).
- Installer improvements: PR-19110 adds stronger preflight messaging for endpoint/DNS prerequisites; not a full fix for NACL issues but reduces time-to-diagnosis.

Comments (condensed)
- 2025-07-08 (Colin O'Donnell, Support): "Customer reports intermittent DNS in private subnets; installer pods failing 'no such host' for STS/ECR. Requesting Infra/Networking eyes."
- 2025-07-08 (Victor Alvarez, Infra): "Please confirm VPC enableDnsHostnames and NACL rules for ephemeral return; seen this manifest as intermittent UDP 53 loss. Also check endpoint SG sources include pod CIDR if using VPC CNI."
- 2025-07-10 (Sean Gallagher, SRE): "CoreDNS metrics show upstream timeouts; recommend scaling CoreDNS and checking for CPU throttling. If packet loss persists, consider NodeLocal DNSCache."
- 2025-07-11 (Colin O'Donnell, Support): "Customer found NACL missing ephemeral return. Applied scoped allow rules + endpoint SG widened to pod CIDR. Monitoring."
- 2025-07-15 (Colin O'Donnell, Support): "72h stable post-change; customer unblocked. Closing as resolved; capturing module doc follow-ups."
resolution: Customer updated NACL to allow UDP/TCP 53 + ephemeral return within VPC CIDR, enabled VPC DNS hostnames, corrected VPC endpoint SG sources to include pod CIDRs, and scaled CoreDNS. DNS instability stopped; installer/image pulls stabilized. Redwood will update alpha module documentation to call out DNS/NACL prerequisites and endpoint SG source guidance.
next_steps: Docs: add DNS/NACL prerequisites + endpoint SG source guidance to alpha deployment guide and reference architecture (owners: Kira Thompson + Victor Alvarez).
Terraform docs: add a troubleshooting section for intermittent DNS and a validation checklist for pilot readiness.
Support playbook: link SUP-28458 pattern under Private/VPC troubleshooting alongside SUP-28411.
